title: Mapping the Dose Threshold of the Benign-Reframing Link in Emergent Misalignment

original_idea.body:
# Dose Threshold of the Benign-Reframing Link in EM

**Problem:** How robust the framing intervention against EM is unknown.

**Direction:** Fine-tune Qwen2.5-Coder under graded framing (none, weak, strong, adversarial), measure EM rate to produce a dose-response curve.

**Why it matters:** Weak framing could silently re-open the EM chain.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2502.17424; arXiv:2506.11613.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Quantifying where the framing defense breaks tells fine-tuners how much framing hygiene is needed.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Graded-framing LoRA fine-tunes on a public dataset; guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: four framing conditions, standard EM eval, dose-response curve.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public dataset and small models; weak lab incentive on framing-robustness follow-up.

low_compute.reasoning: A few small LoRA fine-tunes on a 0.5B-1.5B model; one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Framing-prevents-EM is known; the framing-robustness dose-response may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Framing effect known; robustness dose-response may be open.
